slides.label: Glossary
slides.source_text: Reference · July 2026 snapshot · Back to the talk Basics · cheat sheet Words you'll keep hearing TokenA chunk of text ≈ ¾ of a word. What models read & bill in. PromptThe text you send the model. ContextEverything the model sees in one call — its short-term memory. AgentAn AI that does things in a loop, not just answers. HarnessThe program wrapped around the model — its hands. ConnectorA plug between an AI and another app (Gmail, Drive, Slack…). MCPThe open standard those plugs are built on — "USB-C for AI". CreditsPre-paid units most creative tools bill in — each generation burns some. Generative AIAI that makes media — images, video, voice, music. Deep researchThe AI browses for 5–30 min and returns a cited report. Don't memorise these — each comes back with its own slide. This is just your map.

slides.label: Claude Code and Codex
slides.source_text: Reference · July 2026 snapshot · Back to the talk Big three · the coding agents Claude Code & Codex — the coding agents Claude Code Anthropic's agent for developers: lives in the terminal or editor, reads a whole codebase, writes & runs code, fixes its own mistakes. slides.label: Deep research
slides.source_text: Reference · July 2026 snapshot · Back to the talk In practice · deep research Deep research: one question, a full report Ask one question → the AI browses dozens of sources for 5–30 minutes → returns a multi-page, cited report. Shipped by all three labs (and Perplexity) under roughly this name; included from the ~$20 tiers. Ideal for: market landscapes, competitor teardowns, "what does the research actually say?" Looks right ≠ is right These reports look authoritative and still contain errors. Treat them as a well-organised starting point with a reading list — never a finished document you forward.

slides.label: Perplexity
slides.source_text: Reference · July 2026 snapshot · Back to the talk Landscape · research & search Perplexity — search that shows its sources Ask a question → an answer in prose with citations to live sources — every claim verifiable, not ten blue links. Pro ~$20/mo: unlimited pro search + 20 deep-research runs a day. Enterprise ~$40/seat. Comet — its browser with the assistant built in — went free worldwide in October 2025 (before that, gated behind the $200 Max tier). Careful where it clicks An AI browser acting on pages you're logged into is a documented prompt-injection risk — a hidden instruction on a page can steer it. Keep agentic browsers away from sensitive logged-in systems. Prices ~July 2026.

slides.label: Story 2 · Ten years, two days
slides.source_text: Reference · July 2026 snapshot · Back to the talk Stories · supporting example AI proposed a hypothesis. Scientists supplied the evidence. Hypothesis → validation Imperial College London spent a decade on how superbugs acquire resistance. Google's AI co-scientist, given the same question, ranked the correct — unpublished — answer first in two days. It also proposed a hypothesis the team had never considered. The researchers themselves went on record — this isn't vendor marketing. The honest caveat: the AI generated the hypothesis. Humans had spent the decade doing the lab work that proved it. A generated hypothesis still needs experimental validation.

slides.label: Story 3 · The exams
slides.source_text: Reference · July 2026 snapshot · Back to the talk Stories · supporting example Gold medals, in minutes CFA Level III The hardest finance exam — essays included. Models passed a full mock in minutes (best ~79%). Humans train ~300 hours per level. Maths Olympiad gold Official IMO gold medal, certified by the organisers — 5 of 6 problems, standard conditions. Only ~1 in 10 human contestants got gold. The reframe: the exam-shaped part of professional work — recall, procedure, structured answers — is now cheap. Judgment, accountability, and knowing what to ask are not.

slides.label: Story 4 · The security double
slides.source_text: Reference · July 2026 snapshot · Back to the talk Stories · supporting example The same skill, both directions 🛡 Defence Google's Big Sleep agent found a flaw in software on billions of devices — one only attackers knew — and it was patched before they could strike. A first. ⚔ Offence Anthropic disclosed the first largely AI-orchestrated espionage campaign: a jailbroken coding agent ran ~80–90% of the attack autonomously (Nov 2025). It's the same loop introduced in the main talk doing both jobs. Which one it does is decided by the humans and guardrails around it — which is why the fine-print slides in this deck aren't decoration.

slides.label: The built-ins
slides.source_text: Reference · July 2026 snapshot · Back to the talk Plugging in · the built-ins Or use what's already in the building Microsoft 365 Copilot Agent mode in Word, Excel & PowerPoint — works on the document itself. ~$21–30/user/mo on top of M365. Fun fact: the Office agents run on Anthropic's models. Gemini in Workspace Now bundled into base plans (from ~$14/user) — Gmail, Docs, Meet. Star feature: =AI("prompt", A2) in Sheets — an AI prompt as a formula, filled down 1,000 rows. The trade-off vs the add-ins: built-ins are the path of least resistance (and often the easiest compliance story) — the dedicated tools are usually better at the work itself. Prices July 2026.

slides.label: The universal adapter
slides.source_text: Reference · July 2026 snapshot · Back to the talk Plugging in · the universal adapter The universal adapter for everything else No official connector for your tool? Zapier MCP: one connection exposes ~30,000 actions across 8,000+ apps to Claude or ChatGPT. Setup is paste-a-URL — then just say it: "add this lead to the CRM and post a summary to the channel." Make offers the same on its visual canvas. Both need their own (cheap) plan + a paid AI plan. Expose the minimum The safety rule: plug in only the actions you need. The AI can only misuse what you've connected — keep the adapter's keyring short.
